title: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider
hook: the Provider, of food, work, friends, faith
tomorrow: the owner finally answers. it's a no. or is it?

segments.voice: A week of names. He creates: the plan came first. He brings forth, out of nothing. Shaped by him, every face. Again and again, the door that doesn't lock. Nothing prevails over him. And yesterday's: freely given.
screen: `HE CREATES · HE BRINGS FORTH · SHAPED BY HIM` → `AGAIN AND AGAIN · NOTHING PREVAILS · FREELY GIVEN`

segments.voice: A grocery receipt is a list of provisions, and nobody reads it twice. Yesterday's question was where to start counting, and Dadi Fatima had an answer before Amira finished asking: start with breakfast. Then who drove you. Then who answered your text. Dadi's been doing this out loud at the kitchen table for as long as Amira can remember, and today's name is what she's pointing at.
screen: `NOBODY READS THE RECEIPT.` → `START WITH BREAKFAST.` → `THEN WHO DROVE YOU.`

segments.voice: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider. The Qur'an says it with a kind of emphasis, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah! He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unshakeable might." And it reaches past people: "And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah." The birds are the picture the Prophet, peace be upon him, used. In paraphrase from Tirmidhi: if you relied on Allah as He should be relied on, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds. They go out hungry in the morning and come back full in the evening. Notice the birds still fly out. Provision and effort go together, like the tied camel. And provision is wider than food. Work is provision. A friend who shows up is provision. Faith itself, for the one who has it, is counted among His gifts. This week's names fit together here. The Creator planned; the Maker brought forth; the Fashioner shaped; the Forgiving kept the door open; nothing prevailed over Him; the Bestower gave freely. The Provider keeps it coming, day after day, mostly unnoticed. One to tell a friend tonight: in the hadith, the birds don't stay in the nest waiting. They go out hungry and come back full.
screen: `AR-RAZZAQ: HE GIVETH LIVELIHOOD.` · `EVERY BEAST, EVERY BIRD.` · `OUT HUNGRY, BACK FULL.` · then, large: `HE PROVIDES.`

segments.voice: Do Dadi's count. Start with what you ate today, then who helped you get where you are, then one friend, then one thing you were taught. Touch a finger for each one, and when the fingers run out, start again on the first hand.
Ar-Razzaq: the Provider, of food, work, friends and faith, for every creature down to the birds.
The line for today: he provides, and the birds still fly out to find it. A week of names, held.
